data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root 'r-gh-a', meaning 'to guide'. Marghaa is a name for a messenger or guide in Islam. The name Marghaa carries the meaning “Messenger, Guide” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Marghaa usually hope their child will grow to embody messenger, guide and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the role of a spiritual guide in one's Islamic journey.
data.etymology: Marghaa belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Messenger, Guide.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Marghaa total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, Marghaa embodies the concept of being a guide or a messenger, carrying forth the teachings and wisdom of Islam. The name underscores the importance of individuals connecting with their faith, seeking knowledge, and sharing their understanding with others, ultimately contributing to the spiritual growth of the community. Thus, Marghaa serves as a reminder of one's role in continuing the chain of knowledge and spiritual growth, as well as inspiring those around them to do the same.
